passage: Noa had been sitting on the stairs for twenty minutes with the two halves of the broken blue bowl in her lap. Her friend Hiroshi, waiting by the door with his football, whispered, "Just tell your mum. Mine was cross for one evening, then it was over." Noa stood up and carried the pieces to the kitchen, where her mum was chopping onions. "Mum, I dropped your bowl. I'm so sorry. I was going to hide it." Her mum put the knife down. "Oh, Noa. Thank you for telling me. Are you hurt?" "No." "Then it's only a bowl. We'll see if glue works." Noa's shoulders dropped for the first time all afternoon, and she leaned against her mum.

qa.q: What did Noa carry into the kitchen?
qa.a: She carried the two halves of the broken blue bowl.

qa.q: What was Noa feeling as her talk with Mum ended?
qa.a: Relief. Her shoulders dropped for the first time all afternoon and she leaned against her mum.

qa.q: What could Noa do next to help mend things?
qa.a: She could help try the glue on the bowl, and next time tell her mum sooner instead of waiting on the stairs. 🙂

qa.q: What did Noa's mum seem to care about more than the bowl?
qa.a: She asked first whether Noa was hurt, so Noa's safety and honesty mattered to her more than the bowl.

grounding: Shows a child confessing a mistake to a mother who forgives quickly, giving relief and the sense that it can be mended.
